newsitem.title: NORWAY: Maintenance to hit Norway oil output in Aug - survey.
newsitem.headline: Maintenance to hit Norway oil output in Aug - survey.

text.p: Norwegian crude production will decline around 10 percent in August when several of the largest oilfields are scheduled to close for maintenance, a Reuters survey of oil companies operating in Norwegian waters showed.

Planned shutdowns at Statfjord B and Gullfaks A and B platforms, and the Sleipner East and Troll West developments will reduce output over the month by more than 8.3 million barrels, or an average 267,830 barrels per day (bpd).
In December Norway pumped 3.1 million bpd.
State oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS plans a two-week stoppage at Statfjord B from August 9, which will reduce Statfjord loadings by 2.1 million barrels over the month.
Gullfaks A and B will close for 25 days maintenance from August 25, while the Sleipner East gas and condensate field will shut for 12 days from August 7.
No maintenance was planned for the Heidrun field in the Norwegian Sea but there would be a 24 to 48 hour shutdown before the end of March to repair the platform's flare tip, Statoil said.
Veselefrikk will go into turnaround from June 9 until June 21 and gas production from Troll East will cease from August 4 for 12 days.
Operator of oil-producing Troll West, Norsk Hydro ASA, has scheduled a 14-day shutdown sometime in August.
Two other Hydro-operated fields -- Oseberg and Brage -- will close in June for four and eight days respectively.

Saga Petroleum's Snorre and Tordis will not close during 1997, but the company said its Vigdis development, which is due to come on stream at the beginning of April, will shut for turnaround at the same time as Gullfaks A.
Brief stoppages of a few days are planned British Petroleum's Ula in May, Amoco's Valhall and Hod in March and Elf's Froey.

Norske Shell said upgrading work would continue at Draugen to raise output there to 180,000 bpd. The work is planned to last until mid-year when a decision will be taken as to whether the field requires any further maintenance, a Shell spokesman said.
